So I've looked around at the other ideas on /v/ideasforvoat and I haven't seen this particular rendition come up yet.

Whenever a user downvoats a comment or a submission, they would have to explain why they chose to downvoat that particular piece of content.

I think it can rather be a bit disheartening when you write up a comment to a post or as a response to another user, and find out that it quickly gets downvoated. So you might sit there and wonder if you had been particularly offensive in that post, or was it because someone just had a difference of opinion? And then a thought might arise that this particular person who disagreed with you, might simply not like you.

But in reality, you can't read purpose from a simple "-1". This ambiguity breeds discouragement and discontent. That is why I think it would be particularly helpful if users were required to either explain their reasoning, through simple tags like "spam", "irrelevant information", or other such examples. This would also allow other users to see what was particularly wrong with the users post, and why it might have, or did not deserve the downvoat.

A similar idea was discussed here by /u/sashimi, which I don't think received adequate attention.

Edit: Thanks for the downvoat! I knew it was coming, but could you now tell me why?

I think instead of tagging it as something, which can be abused, an interesting mechanic would be forcing the person to comment on that post saying "I downvoted this post because it does not contribute to the current topic" or whatever reason they downvoted. Another interesting mechanic would be allowing users to disapprove and report invalid downvotes, although this, like tags, could be abused.

Perhaps instead of expecting the world to change in order to accomodate your feelings you might choose to do the reverse. Adjust your thinking to accommodate others behaviour.
